items.caption:
You can dream outside REM sleep too.
In a 2017 sleep-lab study using high-density EEG, people woken from REM and from non-REM sleep reported dreams, and activity in a back-of-brain hot zone tracked whether they dreamed. One lab, so treat it as a strong clue, not the last word.

items.caption:
Can a brain scan guess what you dream?
In a 2013 Science study from Kyoto, a model trained on scans of people looking at pictures picked object categories in sleep-onset imagery from three volunteers, right about 60% of the time on average (chance 50%). Categories, not films.

items.caption:
Teeth falling out in your dreams?
In one study of 210 students, teeth dreams were not linked to psychological distress or general sleep problems, but they did go with tension in the teeth, gums or jaws on waking. Linked, not proven: the authors' idea is that sensations from the mouth can feed into dreams.
